newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends dull session mixed, Sept eases.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends dull session mixed, Sept eases.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mixed in thin choppy trade Friday as light speculative selling was offset by trade buying toward the lows, dealers said.
Locals were seen on both sides of the market, trapping prices in a tight range, they added.
"It was a listless market today," said one trader. "It was one of the smallest ranges we've had in awhile."

Benchmark September arabicas settled down 0.35 cent at 179.50 cents a lb after ranging from 183.50 to 177.50. Spot July finished up 3.05 cents at 198.95, while the outer months closed up 0.45 to down 3.25.
With no notices issued against July as it entered its month-long delivery period today, the July/September switch widened to 19.45 cents at the close, from 16.05 cents on Thursday.
"There is not going to be anything delivered, so the path of least resistance for the switch is up," one traders said.

Coffee prices weakened at the outset, but fell short of the 2.00-cent lower pre-opening call and quickly headed higher. Traders said sentiment on the floor this morning was relatively bullish after Thursday's strong finish.
But the September contract's inability to mount a successful challenge of chart resistance at 185.00 cents prompted selling by locals, they said.

Traders said the market continued to be technically driven, with a dearth of fresh market-moving fundamentals. They continued to peg September resistance at 185.00 cents, with the next upside target at 192.00 cents. Near-term support was seen at 175.00 cents, followed by September's low on Thursday of 168.75 cents.

Some traders said continued mild weather in top-grower Brazil may be discouraging buyers in the short-term. A warm high pressure will build out of northeast Brazil into the coffee belt, promoting warm and dry conditions for most of next week, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Friday.
WSC added, however, that showers and thunderstorms in the next two days will delay and disrupt the Brazilian harvest.
In other news, an official at Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation said he expected the country's 1997/98 coffee crop to come in at about 12 million 60-kg bags.

USDA in its world production report released last week put Colombia's 1997/98 coffee crop at 11.3 million bags, while a statement earlier this week from the London-based Association of Coffee Exporting Countries (ACPC) pegged Colombia's 1997/98 output at up to 15 million bags.
CFTC's Commitments of Traders report due later today is expected to be little changed, traders said.
Volume was thin at an estimated 5,885 lots.
